sentences.text: This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.172/2023 dated 26.08.2023, registered at Police Station - Ahmadpur, Tehsil Shyampur, District Sehore (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 420 and 34 of IPC.
Applicant apprehending her arrest in the aforesaid offence has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
2 . A s per prosecution story, in the year 2013, the present applicant was a Sarpanch of the village and she distributed some pattas without approval of the Tehsildar.
Almost after 10 years, the FIR was registered.
3 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has not committed any offence.
She is innocent and has been falsely implicated.

Learned counsel has drawn attention of the Smt. Laxmi Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123218149/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Court towards Section 244 of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959 prior to 12.02.2020 and has submitted that before 12.02.2020 the day when amendment came into force in the Section 244,
there was specific provision that subject to the rules made in this behalf the Gram Panchayat or where a Gram Panchayat has not been constituted, the Tehsildar shall dispose of sites in the abadi area.
Therefore, it is submitted that no offence is made out.
The applicant being a lady has been implicated for commission of the offence due to political rivalry.
Therefore, he has prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State has submitted that as per the existing law in statute, only Tehsildar has right to dispose of the site is abadi land.
Therefore, she has prayed for rejection of the anticipatory bail.

5. Considering that the FIR has been registered almost after 10 years of the distribution of the pattas and the submission put forth before this Court by learned counsel for the applicant and the relevant provision of Code but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant/accused may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this anticipatory bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant - Smt. Laxmi Bai be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.

(iii) Applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;

(iv) I n case, applicant is not arrested within a period of 10 days' by the Investigation Officer, she shall surrender herself before the Investigation Officer within 7 days'
from today failing which this order shall become ineffective.

7. However, it is being made clear that in case of bail jump and in violation of any of conditions imposed herein above, this order shall become ineffective and Investigation Officer/Trial Court shall be at liberty to proceed against the applicant as per law.
Certified copy as per rules.
